3-603.11
Consumer advisory for consumption of raw or undercooked animal food not adequate.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: If an animal food such as beef, eggs, fish, lamb, milk, pork, poultry, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in ready-to-eat form or as an ingredient in another ready-to-eat food, the permit holder shall inform consumerS of the significantly increased risk of consuming such foods by way of a disclosure and reminder.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Establishment serves a burger with a fried egg. Staff indicated that it is served over-medium with a runny yolk and was unable to say what temperature the eggs are cooked at. Discussed placing a consumer advisory on the menu. Inspector will email Consumer Advisory handout to manager. The establishment must update the menu within 10 days and email a copy of it to the inspector for verification.
3-302.11
Cross-contamination with raw animal products not adequately prevented in storage, preparation, holding, and display.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTIONCorrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: All foods must be stored or prepared according to the final required minimum cooking temperature. In temperature (low to high) order this would be: cooked and ready-to-eat foods, whole muscle fish and meats, ground and injected meat, raw eggs and raw poultry.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed raw shelled eggs and raw chicken stored above vegetable burgers in the low two-door reach-in cooler in Liberty Burger. Observed two trays of raw meatballs stored above a cooked and cooling pan of meatloaf on a baking pan in the Tanglewood kitchen. Staff moved these items around at time of inspection. This will be marked as corrected on site.
5-205.11
Handwashing sink used for purposes other than handwashing.
Corrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: A handwashing sink may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed a whisk in the Liberty Burger handwashing sink. Staff indicated that some food equipment are also rinsed out in the sink. Observed a sign above the sink that indicated that the sink is for handwashing use only. Observed equipment stored in the handwashing sink located in the dishpit area. of the Tanglewood kitchen. No paper towels were observed in this area. Observed a sign above the sink that indicated that the sink is for handwashing use only. Discussed that handwashing sinks cannot be used for purposes other than handwashing and that they must always be stocked with soap and paper towels. Staff moved the items at time of inspection. This will be marked as corrected on site.
3-501.16
Hot time/temperature control for safety food not adequately temperature controlled.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTIONCorrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be hot held at 57 degrees C (135 degrees F) or above.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Measured cooked mushrooms being hot held on the flattop to be at 113F. Staff voluntarily discarded the item at time of inspection. This will be marked as corrected on site. Additionally observed cooked bacon hot held on the flattop. The bacon was at 76F. Discussed that fully cooked, crispy bacon can be considered shelf-stable, however, some bacon pieces appeared soft. Discussed ensuring that the bacon are fully cooked and crispy or using time or temperature as a control.
3-501.16
Cold time/temperature control for safety food not adequately temperature controlled.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTIONCorrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be cold held at 5 degrees C (41 degrees F) or less. Eggs shall be stored at a temperature of 7 degrees C (45 degrees F) or less.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Measured several time/temperature control for safety food items above 41F. Items were queso blanco, cooked hashbrowns, and sauces that ranged in temperature from 62F to 68F. See Temperature Observations for full list. Staff voluntarily discarded these items at time of inspection. This will be marked as corrected on site.
4-901.11
Utensils not adequately air dried or cloth dried.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils: shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food; and may not be cloth dried except that utensils that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are maintained clean and dry.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed stacked equipment that were still wet in the Tanglewood and Merry Piglets kitchens. Discussed the above recommended resolution. Staff indicated that the Merry Piglets kitchen is used for washing dishes. Additionally discussed that Liberty Burger was approved to use the Tanglewood kitchen for dishes- not Merry Piglets. The establishment must ensure that all equipment and utensils are air dried immediately. Email inspector protocol within 14 days.
3-501.17
Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety food improperly date marked.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. The day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer's use-by date.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed several ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods without datemarking. Discussed the above recommended resolution. The establishment must review with staff datemarking protocol and email written verification to inspector within 10 days of what the protocol is.
